why: P280 is the first prospective test in this program, and the first run where the external dependency itself blocked the design (the ARK CodingPlan subscription expired mid-run; the VLM was switched to Command Code / glm-5.3-flash and all rows were re-collected with one model). The record pins the two checks that keep the result honest: an independent recompute of the template stage, and a design gate that refuses to score a decimated input.

independent_recompute.estimator: from-scratch NCC matcher; does not import p280_run.py

perturbation_test.perturbation: decimate the raw file to 2 evaluable rows and run the real p280_verdict.py
perturbation_test.expected: design gate fires -> overall INCOMPLETE, every prediction NOT SCORED

validity_clauses: fewer than two valid templates -> row non-evaluable
fewer than 4 evaluable rows -> INCOMPLETE, nothing scored
bbox stability gate: two temperature-0 calls per object, IoU >= 0.90 or the object is dropped
declared_deviations: 5 evaluable rows instead of the designed 6 (Cloth1's object-list call returned a single object)
VLM switched from doubao-seed-2.1-lite to z-ai/glm-5.3-flash after the ARK CodingPlan subscription expired; Baby2's first-round cache was deleted so all rows use one model
scene list amended before the run: Art and Dolls are not in the 2006 FullSize set; frozen list is Baby2 / Cloth1 / Cloth2

result.P280-1: FAIL — R2 median 0.1212 vs R1 0.1619 (both under the bar in the median) but the paired comparison is 2 wins / 2 losses / 1 tie, exact sign test p = 0.6875 (ties dropped, n = 4): the in-sample cluster advantage did not transfer
result.P280-2: PASS — the majority-background class survives: Cloth1 and Cloth2 both keep rel_err >= 0.15 under R1 AND R2
result.P280-3: PASS — random selection fails 2 of 5 rows (0.2353, 0.6972), so the control is discriminative here, unlike P279's cohort
